title: The Garden That Closes
mathematical_role: Exhibit one exact finite union-closed family and make closure plus the global frequency question visible.
learning_objective: Read an explicit family, verify representative unions, and compare exact element frequencies with the half threshold without mistaking one example for a proof.
literal_semantics: F = {∅,{a},{b},{a,b},{a,c},{a,b,c}} is the finite family depicted.
nonliteral_semantics: Node spacing and edge geometry do not encode metric or probabilistic information.

notes: Exact finite-example data are reproduced by tests/test_visual_pedagogy_batch1_candidates.py.
Imported theorem-terrain language remains bounded by the documentary source and does not admit a new external claim.

renderer.version_or_environment: Python 3 standard library; deterministic SVG generator v1
reproducibility_notes: The generator uses no network, randomness, timestamps, fonts embedded as files, or external data.
Repository tests compare generator output byte-for-byte with the committed SVG candidate.

accessibility.alt_text: Exact six-set union-closed family arranged by inclusion, with a frequency ledger showing a in four sets, b in three, c in two, and the half threshold at three.
accessibility.long_description: The candidate depicts F={∅,{a},{b},{a,b},{a,c},{a,b,c}} as a finite inclusion diagram. Representative unions are written explicitly. A frequency ledger gives counts 4, 3, and 2 for a, b, and c; because |F|=6, the Frankl threshold is 3, so a and b satisfy it in this example.

claim_boundary.strongest_visual_claim: For the explicitly displayed six-set family, the shown unions, frequencies, and half threshold are exact.
not_claimed: Frankl's union-closed sets conjecture in general
A classification of all union-closed families
A proof that the displayed edges are a complete Hasse diagram beyond the exact family semantics

supersession_reason: Replace the metaphorical garden grammar with one exact six-set union-closed example that exposes pairwise unions and exact element frequencies.
